:::{#thm-null-space-subspace}
#### A null space is a subspace

For any $m \times n$ matrix $\matr{A}$,
$\mathcal{N}(\matr{A})$ (@def-null-space)
is a subspace of $\reals^n$ (@def-subspace).

:::

::: proof

$\matr{A} \vzero_n = \vzero_m$, so $\vzero_n \in \mathcal{N}(\matr{A})$,
and the null space is not empty.
If $\vecf{u}, \vecf{w} \in \mathcal{N}(\matr{A})$ and $c \in \reals$, then

$$
\ba
\matr{A}\,(\vecf{u} + \vecf{w})
&= \matr{A} \vecf{u} + \matr{A} \vecf{w}
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-distrib)}
\\
&= \vzero_m + \vzero_m
&& \text{(} \vecf{u} \text{ and } \vecf{w} \text{ are in the null space)}
\\
&= \vzero_m
&& \text{(adding } \vzero_m \text{ changes nothing)}
\ea
$$

and, for each entry $i = 1, \ldots, m$,

$$
\ba
\paren{\matr{A}\,(c \vecf{u})}_i
&= a_{i1} (c u_1) + \cdots + a_{in} (c u_n)
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\
&= c\,(a_{i1} u_1 + \cdots + a_{in} u_n)
&& \text{(factor } c \text{ out of each term)}
\\
&= c\,(\matr{A} \vecf{u})_i
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\
&= c \cd 0
&& \text{(} \vecf{u} \text{ is in the null space)}
\\
&= 0,
&& \text{(arithmetic)}
\ea
$$

so $\matr{A}\,(c \vecf{u}) = \vzero_m$.
Therefore $\vecf{u} + \vecf{w}$ and $c \vecf{u}$ are in $\mathcal{N}(\matr{A})$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-null-space-subspace}
#### The solutions of $\matr{A} \vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$ with $\vecf{b} \neq \vzero$ are not a subspace

In @exm-null-space, $(2, 1, 0)$ and $(2, 0, 1)$ are in $\mathcal{N}(\matr{A})$,
and so is their sum $(4, 1, 1)$,
since $4 - 2 \cd 1 - 2 \cd 1 = 0$.
By contrast, the solutions of
$\matr{A} \vecf{x} = (1, 3)$ for the same $\matr{A}$
are the vectors with $x_1 - 2x_2 - 2x_3 = 1$.
That set does not contain $\vzero_3$,
so by @thm-subspace-zero it is not a subspace.

:::
